A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HaMI, and their supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, v1 refers to Mistral supplementary results that are absent from its nine-page PDF, limiting that comparison. All three appendices supplied in v2 were inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, ablations and token-level examples in Section 5, Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations and sensitivity experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B, including evaluations with three LLM configurations.

M1.justification: The central selection procedure changes from a single maximum-scoring token and hinge-style MIL loss to top-k selection and an objective using norms of averaged selected scores (Section 4.1). v2 makes k depend on response length. Representation augmentation also changes from two adjustable coefficients to a fixed unit coefficient plus one uncertainty weight; the smoothness term remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate context-free, zero-shot QA hallucination detection on Trivia QA, SQuAD, NQ and BioASQ, including transfer among these datasets. Different LLM configurations change experimental settings. Appendix C's summarization application is proposed without evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MARS, MARS-SE and CCS, removes RMD and the generic LP-First/LP-Last entries, and reports an explicitly configured SAPLMA correctness probe. The cross-dataset comparator set also changes. In the token-selection comparison, v2 Table 2 replaces the Mean comparator from v1 Table 3 with Before Last.

E3.justification: The main evaluations replace LLaMA-2-chat-7B/13B with LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-Nemo-12B and an 8-bit 70B LLaMA. Training sampling changes from 3,000 to 2,000 pairs, temperature from 0.9 to 0.5, and labeling from GPT-4 to GPT-4.1. Test selection changes from 400 sampled questions to 500 before filtering to approximately 400. Added experiments vary detector architecture, augmentation strength and token-selection fraction.

E4.justification: v2 adds detector-width/depth, augmentation-strength and top-k-fraction studies, and expands layer analysis from two datasets to four. Token-selection and uncertainty ablations change from four datasets with one LLM to two datasets with two LLMs. However, v1 Table 2's component combinations and isolated smoothness-loss ablation disappear. The Figure 4 token examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. Both present point AUROC estimates. Six-answer sampling and averaging cross-dataset evaluations remain unchanged reporting practices.

E6.justification: Main, transfer and ablation results are extensively replaced, and sensitivity results are added. For example, Table 1 reports HaMI Trivia QA AUROC of 0.923 with LLaMA-2-chat-7B in v1 versus 0.897 with LLaMA-3.1-8B in v2; changed conditions prevent interpreting this as a performance decline. v2 also adds Mistral, 70B and HaMI* result blocks. HaMI remains first-ranked throughout Table 1.

T1.justification: The formal development receives localized revisions: v2 defines the ordered top-k index set, reformulates the MIL objective using selected-score averages, and defines length-dependent k in Appendix B. The underlying MIL assumptions and smoothness formulation remain. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims: novel joint token selection and hallucination detection through MIL, uncertainty-enhanced representations, and robust superiority on four QA benchmarks. Revised experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly states the internal-representation access requirement and limitations of simple uncertainty fusion, and sketches a summarization adaptation through sentence-level entailment. Section 5.3 revises the generation-length interpretation and qualifies token-level uncertainty as having limited effectiveness, replacing v1's uniformly positive interpretation of the three uncertainty enhancements.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and substantial implementation disclosure: MLP dimensions, BatchNorm/ReLU/sigmoid components, Adam, software versions, A100 hardware, validation-based layer selection, labeling prompts and runtime costs including semantic-uncertainty overhead. These details do not establish changes to previously undisclosed implementation choices. A remaining ambiguity is the 70B model's inconsistent designation as 3.3 in Table 1 and 3.13 in prose.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion covering MARS, follow-up-question lie detection, and recent attention/internal-representation research. These broaden the examples and contextual support within the existing uncertainty-versus-internal-representations taxonomy. The central positioning around joint token selection and detection remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained. v2 refines terminology and prose, rewrites selected related-work and experimental-discussion paragraphs, makes the experimental setup unnumbered, and organizes additional material into Appendices A–C. Much of the abstract, introduction and methodological explanation remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Table 1 gains a third LLM block and colored rankings; token and uncertainty tables become paired panels. Figures 3 and 5 gain sensitivity panels, Figure 2 is updated for top-k selection, and appendix prompt and tuning figures are added. Figures 1 and 4 are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency and empirical scrutiny through implementation and validation details, runtime accounting, expanded baseline comparisons, and architecture, augmentation and selection sensitivity studies. These gains are tempered by removing v1's isolated smoothness-loss ablation and mean-pooling control, weakening component validation. With the main claims retained and performance measured under revised settings, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
